items.title: Sumner Labat Interview, 1962-11-11
items.q: He was Raymond Perkins Paul Crawford right now.

ctx.x: Yeah. I go around and listen to bands in this French Quarter. Listen to that cellar stare at them there after I get off from work, you know, sometimes. See, I get off early, I say, I'm going to the French Quarter, listen to that some good jazz music. And what's that white band, the Orphanile, they've been a while in the Orange. Sharky? No, I've been a Sharky too. Dukes of Dixon Land? Dukes of Dixon Land, that was my favorite. They were good during that time. And Famous Doors. Yeah. Yeah, that's where they're…

We're missing that piano player right now. He's playing with Raymond. Raymond Boyd. He was Raymond Perkins Paul Crawford right now. Yeah. The piano player quit him and came back, you know. He got tired of being away from home. Oh.
Uh huh. Yeah. They had a real Dixieland band though. Couldn't take it from them. I was a young brother. Very good. The old man did the poem they band, I read. He plays the trombone.
